I guess something may be leaking -- putting `contrib.postgres` stuff outside of `postgres_tests` seems like a candidate though I haven't though about the reason for that.

It looks like some tests is are leaking a `TIME_ZONE!='America/Chicago'` which causes `HumanizeTests.test_naturalday_uses_localtime` settings override to require a database connection. It's not clear to me why these tests don't use `timezone.override` just like we do with `translations` which have no effect on database connections.

Alright, I'd suggest keeping the `contrib.postgres` tests in `postgres_tests`. Maybe under a new `test_schema` module. In call cases you'll want to make sure to subclass `postgres_tests.PostgreSQLTestCase` which makes sure to disconnect the `register_type_handlers` `connection_created` receiver and is causing all the failures here.

I'll see if I can come up with a PR that automatically unregister the signal when `'django.contrib.postgres'` is removed from `INSTALLED_APPS` but I still believe these tests should live in `postgres_tests`.

I agree. I think the main issue is trying to reuse the `SchemaTests` class. That relates to how to  [organize test utilities](https://groups.google.com/d/topic/django-developers/mfuo0sOF2Xo/discussion). I think postgres_tests shouldn't import a base class from the schema app, right?

> That relates to how to organize test utilities. I think postgres_tests shouldn't import a base class from the schema app, right?

Right, importing stuff between test apps should be avoided. It would be great if components such as schema editor, contrib apps with backends, core backends, would expose some base classes/mixins that third party apps (and ourselves in the test suite) could rely on.

As an example, I recently had to work on a project shipping it's own session backend. Being able to import `session_tests.tests.SessionTestsMixin` through `django.contrib.session.test.utils.SessionBackendTestsMixin` would have made it easy to assert the backend was appropriately working between Django versions without having to embed the source into the project.

Given the large number of third-party custom backends around I think this idea has merit as it would allow developers to make sure their backend comply with a set of expectations. For example, the `django-redis-session` backend is moderately popular but doesn't implement, [or at least test against](https://github.com/martinrusev/django-redis-sessions/blob/f2baa7efaed11b7e43fda7c72ee9426461547205/tests/tests.py), the latest session reuse security tweaks shipped in recent Django versions.

Another case would be for testing utilities. Wouldn't be great if `contrib.messages` provided some testing abstraction (e.g. `MessagesTestMixin.assertSuccesMessage(response, msg)`) so you don't have to manually check against `response.context['messages']` to figure out whether or not a message was sent by your view.

Anyway this is not the best channel to communicate this. I'll try to replay to your django-dev thread.

Regarding the `setting_changed` tweak PoC it can be reviewed in #9353. This is really a hack because we don't have any _uninstall_ hook on app configs but it seems to be working pretty well.
